title: Endace ERF Interface Id extension
description:
The Endace ERF format has extended the 'Interface Id' from 2 bits (interface 0-3) to 3 bits (interface 0-7).
The Interface Id high order bit is not adjacent in the flags field.

Extend wtap handling for ERF records.
Extend epan dissection and display of ERF format.
The existing erf.flags.cap field is retained and extended to 0-7.
A new erf.flags.if_raw field is added for the unformatted value.

Note proto_tree_add_split_bits_item_ret_val() cannot be used here because it only supports input from the tvb and not from a non-tvb value.

Is this just a generic receive error, or is it specifically a receive checksum error?

This is more a packet capture error, as is DS Error. It may not correlate with a checksum error, so the assigned group is inaccurate.
Which PI event group is most suitable? PI_PROTOCOL? It's not specifically a protocol violation either.
Could we have a PI_CAPTURE, PI_FAULT, or PI_HARDWARE group maybe?

So the ERF Types document I have says that an "RX error" is

> RX error. The number of packets received on this port with an error. Errors can be: FCS, short packet, truncated packet, length field, length type, frame code, or frame invalid errors. Present on the wire.

and a "DS error" is

> DS error. An internal error generated inside the DAG card annotator.  
> Not present on the wire.
> 
> On the DAG 9.2SX2, 9.2X2 and 10X series cards, this error represents a port drop inside the internal data path.

So an "RX error" is sort of the "or" of several of the "link-layer-dependent errors" in the Enhanced Packet Block Flags Word in pcapng.  Perhaps `PI_RECEIVE_ERROR` or something such as that; we already have `PI_CHECKSUM`, which we use for various checksum errors *above* the link layer; with `PI_RECEIVE_ERROR`, there might be some debate about which category a *link-layer* checksum error should go into - I might be tempted to separate checksum errors from symbol error/preamble error/Start Frame Delimiter error/unaligned frame error/wrong Inter Frame Gap error/packet too short error/packet too long error/etc., although "RX error" could either be a checksum error or one of the other errors, so maybe `PI_RECEIVE_ERROR` should be used for all link-layer receive errors.

"DS error" could be in an "adapter error" category (i.e., it's a problem internal to the adapter, not a problem with the packet as received).  We could add a `PI_ADAPTER` event group for that.

We have a separate severity field to distinguish between ERROR, WARNING, INFO etc, so perhaps the category name should not include _ERROR, but instead be PI_RECEIVE, PI_CAPTURE, or PI_LINK? This is for real 'errors on the wire' including short frames etc, potentially including L2 checksums.
Agreed we can add PI_ADAPTER or similar for internal capture system errors/info (not on the wire).

> perhaps the category name should not include \_ERROR

You're right, it shouldn't.  Severity and category are separate attributes of an expert info.
So maybe `PI_RECEIVE`, for receive indications of any sort.

Agreed. So PI_RECEIVE for wire/link expert info, and PI_ADAPTER to distinguish non-wire 'capture system' related expert info?
This could be used for information such as link rate changes, timestamp clock synchronisation etc as well as capture hardware/firmware errors.

> So PI_RECEIVE for wire/link expert info, and PI_ADAPTER to distinguish non-wire 'capture system' related expert info?

Yes.  Should I add those in a separate merge request?

> This could be used for information such as link rate changes

That also indicates that pcapng should have a way to indicate interface property changes (link rate, network address, etc.).

If you have time that would be great.

Alternatively I can raise a separate MR for that and rebase this.

> That also indicates that pcapng should have a way to indicate interface property changes (link rate, network address, etc.).

Could be interesting to have pcapng generate a new/updated IDB? Also could generate these EI from radiotap header info.

> If you have time that would be great.

Working on it.

Should it be `PI_ADAPTER` or `PI_INTERFACE`? Indications will *probably* be generated by hardware adapters, but some interfaces implemented in software could provide indications as well.
PI_INTERFACE might make more sense? Information might come from a NPB trailer or ERSPAN header for instance, so might not always be 'network adapter card'.
!14255 adds `PI_RECEIVE` and `PI_INTERFACE`.
Done.
Should those two bits have different expert infos?
Do we need separate expert_field entries for each to maintain separate counts? I can add additional ones for unique error bits.

> Do we need separate expert_field entries for each to maintain separate counts?

To maintain different expert info types for people to filter on, yes - not just separate counts.

But if something isn't a checksum error, it shouldn't be reported as such.  *Neither* of those are guaranteed to be checksum errors - even RX errors aren't - so perhaps `ei_erf_rx_error` and `ei_erf_ds_error`?

(If the adapter and software could report, and the file format could indicate, individual receive error types, rather than just "some type of receive error", that would help here.)

commits_data.message:
Endace ERF Interface Id extension

The Endace ERF format has extended the 'Interface Id' from 2 bits (interface 0-3) to 3 bits (interface 0-7).
The Interface Id high order bit is not adjacent in the flags field.

Extend wtap handling for ERF records.
Extend epan dissection and display of ERF format.
The existing erf.flags.cap field is retained and extended to 0-7.
A new erf.flags.if_raw field is added for the unformatted value.

Note proto_tree_add_split_bits_item_ret_val() cannot be used here because it only supports input from the tvb and not from a non-tvb value.
